review_notes: I read the whole file and the definitions it uses: candidateLow/High/Lag/Quotient, endpointSplitWeight, candidateMeanWeight and candidateMeanWeight_eq. I also compared it with its sibling CandidateRowMajorant.lean. The only simp-interface issue I found is the repeated manual unfolding in the first theorem. It is a modest finding. I did not look for competing simp rules, because the file declares no simp attributes and its `simp_rw [mul_sum]` is local. I could not run Lean. I did not check whether `dsimp` actually reduces `∏ p ∈ e.2.1, p` back to `candidateLow e` after a rewrite, so the orientation proposed below is unverified. A finding on the second theorem's `simp_rw [mul_sum]` would be speculative, so I did not report one.

findings.problem: There is no canonical rewrite from candidateMeanWeight to the endpointSplitWeight product. Each proof therefore unfolds `endpointSplitWeight`, `candidateLow` and `candidateHigh` by hand with `dsimp`, then closes with `ring`. The identical line `dsimp [d,endpointSplitWeight,candidateLow,candidateHigh]` is also in CandidateRowMajorant.lean line 36, and `candidateLow`/`candidateHigh` are unfolded the same way in at least three other JointDickman files. `candidateMeanWeight_eq` is stated with raw `regularCoefficientWeight (candidateLow e) * regularResidueWeight …` factors. The same quantity is stated with `endpointSplitWeight` in this file's conclusion. The two forms are bridged only by ad hoc definitional unfolding. The proof therefore depends on the unfolding set and on `ring` matching atoms. The unfolding of `candidateLow` is also the wrong direction for the target statement, because it exposes `∏ p ∈ e.2.1, p`, which is `candidateLow e` itself.
findings.proposed_change: Add one lemma next to `endpointSplitWeight`, or next to `candidateMeanWeight_eq`. It would say `candidateMeanWeight B L τ C S χ e = independentRootMean B L τ C / B * (endpointSplitWeight B L τ C (S e.1.1) e.2.1 * endpointSplitWeight B L τ C (S e.1.2) e.2.2 * regularCoefficientWeight B L τ C (candidateQuotient e)) * χ e`. It would be proved once, using the unfold-and-`ring` argument that now appears in the two majorant files. Optionally mark it `@[simp]`, or make it the canonical form of `candidateMeanWeight_eq`. Both majorant proofs could then use `rw` of this lemma plus `ring`/`mul_assoc`, with no `dsimp` of `candidateLow` or `candidateHigh`. Alternatively add `endpointSplitWeight_def` as a `rfl` unfolding lemma and `candidateLow_def`/`candidateHigh_def`, so that proofs do not unfold to raw products.
findings.benefit: The two majorant theorems (forward and reverse) share one maintained bridge between `candidateMeanWeight` and `endpointSplitWeight`. Proofs no longer depend on `dsimp` unfolding order or on `ring` matching `∏` atoms. Later changes to the definitions of `candidateLow`, `candidateHigh` or `endpointSplitWeight` need only one fix.
